audit_findings.title: Post-FY2025 acquisition financing is outside the OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,500.8m acquisition price; $7,259.6m June 2026 total debt; $40.5m nine-month acquisition/Tennessee financing costs; acquired business contributed $44.8m quarterly revenue and a $6.9m net loss
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE numerator excludes the acquired operation and most post-year-end financing costs, while the June 2026 bridge reflects the resulting debt and hybrid securities.
audit_findings.evidence: The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of calendar 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by the TPUC.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch. The acquisition closed March 31, 2026 and was financed after FY2025. Missing Tennessee OE could understate value, while missing recurring interest and hybrid costs could overstate it. These filed amounts are comparable to or larger than the modeled operating values of $1,507m-$2,347m, so the valuation conclusion cannot be relied upon without alignment.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on one dated perimeter: include Spire Tennessee's recurring OE, all acquisition-related interest and junior-subordinated-note costs, and applicable dilution; also remove operations sold before the valuation date. Alternatively, use a consistently pre-transaction balance sheet, claims and operating perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Preferred dividends may be missing from common-shareholder OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.8m annual preferred dividends; conditional modeled effect of $157.5m-$245.3m, or $2.64-$4.11 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If consolidated OE was calculated before preferred dividends, the numerator values cash belonging to the preferred claim while the denominator contains only common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the terms of the Preferred Stock, the Company’s ability to declare or pay dividends on, or purchase or redeem, shares of its common stock or any class or series of capital stock of the Company that rank junior to the Preferred Stock are subject to certain restrictions in the event that the Company does not declare and pay the full cumulative dividends on the Preferred Stock through the most recently completed quarterly dividend period.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the $14.8m dividend was omitted is unresolved because the OE workpaper is not supplied. Even assuming the entire annual amount was omitted from the $141.6m loss anchor, linear scenario scaling would reduce values by only $2.64-$4.11 per share; every scenario would remain materially negative versus the $82.68 market price. The preferred stock was also redeemed in February 2026, although its replacement financing belongs in the current-perimeter rerun addressed separately.
audit_findings.action: Trace FY2019-FY2025 OE to net income available to common shareholders or financing cash flows. Correct any historical omission, then ensure the current-perimeter rerun substitutes the recurring cost of the replacement junior subordinated financing without double counting.

audit_findings.title: A timing-distorted negative year is compounded indefinitely
audit_findings.magnitude: $399.2m OE decline from 2024 to 2025; bull operating PV is $840.0m below bear and bull value is $14.10 per share below bear
audit_findings.mechanism: Percentage growth applied to the negative $141.6m anchor enlarges the loss, lowering OE, terminal value and equity value as the assumed growth rate rises.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition to the changes in net income between the respective periods (discussed in the “Earnings” section above), the remaining changes were related to regulatory timing and fluctuations in working capital items, as discussed below in the Future Cash Requirements section.
audit_findings.explanation: The inverted scenario ordering is a demonstrated modeling error: 6% growth produces a more negative value than negative 2% growth. The filing also attributes the operating-cash-flow movement to regulatory timing and working-capital fluctuations, but it does not quantify the reversible portion of the OE loss. Because correcting the anchor and recovery path could reverse the sign and conclusion, this remains material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $399.2m OE swing to regulatory assets and liabilities, receivables, inventories, payables and other working-capital movements. Normalize only filed or otherwise demonstrated reversals, then rerun with explicit bear, base and bull paths toward normalized OE rather than percentage growth applied to a negative number.

audit_findings.title: Growth investment may be classified as maintenance capital
audit_findings.mechanism: Deducting rate-base expansion, new-business connections or other growth investment as maintenance capex depresses OE without recognizing the associated future regulated earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: However, total capital expenditures were $61.1 higher than last year, with a $125.7 spending increase in the Utilities driven by infrastructure upgrades, advanced meter installations, and new business offset by a $64.5 spending decrease for Midstream.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies a $125.7m increase in Utility spending driven by a mixture of infrastructure upgrades, advanced meters and new business, but it does not separate sustaining expenditure from growth investment. The amount potentially misclassified therefore cannot be established. Given the negative anchor and $922.4m total FY2025 capital expenditure, a meaningful classification error could affect value, but materiality is unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the asset-level maintenance-capex schedule and reconcile it to the $922.4m filed total. Classify replacements and mandated sustaining work separately from capacity, customer-growth and rate-base projects, and rerun OE only for amounts supported by that evidence while treating related future earnings consistently.

audit_findings.title: One-time acquisition costs may be perpetuated in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.4m after tax, equal to 8.1% of the absolute anchor; conditional modeled lift of $121.3m-$189.0m, or $2.03-$3.17 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in FY2025 OE, a non-recurring transaction charge is embedded in every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The major contributor to this variance was the $14.9 pre-tax ($11.4 after-tax) increase in acquisition and restructuring activities due to our recently announced Piedmont Tennessee acquisition, combined with the $8.2 ($6.3 after-tax) interest rate swap gain in the prior year that did not repeat.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention in the OE workpaper is unresolved. Even if the full filed $11.4m after-tax amount were added back to the anchor, proportional scenario scaling would lift value by only $2.03-$3.17 per share, leaving bear, base and bull values approximately negative $22.90, $30.34 and $35.86 per share. It therefore cannot change the present negative-versus-$82.68 conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2025 OE workpaper for the acquisition and restructuring charge. If retained, rerun after removing only the documented non-recurring $11.4m after-tax amount while retaining recurring integration, transition and financing costs.
